name: Black Holes of Anti-de Sitter Space with Three Charges
description: Static black holes of anti-de Sitter space in five dimensions with three electric charges and two scalar fields, found by Klaus Behrndt, Mirjam Cvetič, and Wafic Sabra in the STU model of gauged supergravity, with horizons that are 3-spheres, flat, or hyperbolic. Lifted to ten dimensions the charges are spins of D3-branes, and the supersymmetric solutions are superstars, naked singularities whose sources are giant gravitons.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, with the Ricci tensor the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$. The radius $L$ of anti-de Sitter space is a length, and the parameters $\mu$ and $q_i$ are lengths squared.
history: In the gauged supergravity of five dimensions the scalar fields have a potential, and at its minimum the vacuum of the theory is anti-de Sitter space [behrndt1999]. Klaus Behrndt, Ali Chamseddine, and Wafic Sabra solved its Killing spinor equations for static black holes with electric charge in July 1998, and wrote that "none of them possess a regular horizon" [behrndt1998bps]. In one family of their solutions the metric functions stay finite at $r = 0$, and the geometry continues past it to a naked singularity "only a finite distance away" [behrndt1998bps]. To overcome that, they wrote, "one should consider the non-extremal case" [behrndt1998bps].¶Behrndt, Mirjam Cvetič, and Sabra then found the nonextremal holes, which "differ from those in the ungauged supergravity only in the non-extremality function" [behrndt1999]. In the STU model, whose three scalars $S$, $T$, and $U$ obey $STU = 1$, they wrote the solution out, and it solves the gauged supergravities with $N = 4$ and $N = 8$ as well [behrndt1999]. Each of three electric charges enters through a function $H_i = 1 + q_i/r^2$, and the metric function is $$f = k - \frac{\mu}{r^2} + \frac{r^2}{L^2}H_1H_2H_3,$$ with $\mu$ the nonextremality parameter, $L$ the radius of anti-de Sitter space, and $k = 1$, $0$, or $-1$ for a horizon that is a 3-sphere, flat, or hyperbolic [behrndt1999, cvetic1999phases]. The two scalar fields enter through $X_i = (H_1H_2H_3)^{1/3}/H_i$, whose product is one [behrndt1999, cvetic1999embed]. The term in $L$ comes from the gauging, and with $L \to \infty$ the metric is the black hole of flat space with three charges [behrndt1999].¶With $\mu = 0$ the solution is supersymmetric and its singularity naked, so a black hole needs $\mu$ above a bound, which Behrndt, Cvetič, and Sabra found from a cubic equation in $r^2$ [behrndt1999]. At the bound the inner and outer horizons meet, and the hole has zero temperature and a finite entropy with no supersymmetry [behrndt1999]. Its mass, with Newton's constant set to $G = \pi/4$, is $M = q_1 + q_2 + q_3 + \frac{3}{2}\mu$ [behrndt1999]. With equal charges the scalars are constant, and the hole is then the Reissner-Nordström-anti-de Sitter black hole of five dimensions [myers2001]. The hole with no charge is the Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter black hole of five dimensions, whose temperature has its minimum, $\sqrt{2}/\pi L$ in natural units, at $\mu = 3L^2/4$ [behrndt1999, cvetic1999phases].¶Cvetič and Steven Gubser showed in February 1999 that the region near a stack of D3-branes spinning in one plane reduces on its 5-sphere to the hole with one charge and a flat horizon, $k = 0$ [cvetic1999phases]. They called the charges R-charges, since the rotations of the 5-sphere are the R-symmetry of the gauge theory on the branes [cvetic1999phases]. Cvetič and Gubser asked "What happens in a quantum theory of gravity when a black hole becomes thermodynamically unstable?", and these holes become unstable when their charges grow too large [cvetic1999phases]. At fixed electric potentials they found unstable holes whose action is still below that of empty anti-de Sitter space, and suggested that such a hole might break into several [cvetic1999phases]. At fixed charges, empty anti-de Sitter space has the smaller action wherever the hole is unstable [cvetic1999phases].¶Cvetič and nine coauthors embedded the whole theory in type IIB supergravity on the 5-sphere a month later, so that every solution of it lifts to ten dimensions [cvetic1999embed]. In ten dimensions the three charges are angular momenta of the 5-sphere in three orthogonal planes [cvetic1999embed, cvetic1999phases]. The hole with a flat horizon is the region near D3-branes spinning in all three, with $q_i = \ell_i^2$ for rotation parameters $\ell_i$, and its horizon lies on the world volume of the branes [cvetic1999embed]. Robert C. Myers and Øyvind Tafjord called the solutions with $\mu = 0$ superstars in 2001, since they have no horizon [myers2001]. With one charge the horizon shrinks to zero size as $\mu \to 0$ and the singularity at $r = 0$ is null, and with two or three charges a gap in $\mu$ separates the superstar from the black holes, and its singularity is timelike [myers2001]. For three charges ordered $q_1 \ge q_2 \ge q_3$ the geometry continues past $r = 0$, and in the radius $\rho$ with $\rho^2 = r^2 + q_3$ the singularity lies at $\rho = 0$ [myers2001].¶In ten dimensions Myers and Tafjord found a dipole of the 5-form field at the singularity and traced it to spherical D3-branes on the 5-sphere, giant gravitons, $Nq_1/L^2$ of them for one charge with $N$ units of 5-form flux [myers2001]. The giant gravitons of three charges form three separate collections, each moving around the 5-sphere along its own angle [myers2001]. Jan Gutowski and Harvey Reall found supersymmetric black holes of anti-de Sitter space in five dimensions with regular horizons in 2004, with the three charges equal, and their angular momentum, equal in two orthogonal planes, "can never vanish" [gutowski2004]. Dam T. Son and Andrei O. Starinets found that for the holes with a flat horizon the ratio of shear viscosity to entropy density in the gauge theory is $1/4\pi$, with $\hbar = k_B = 1$, at every chemical potential [son2006]. Liam Gladden, Victor Ivo, Pavel Kovtun, and Starinets showed that the holes with a flat horizon are thermodynamically unstable at low temperature, and with three equal charges the differences between the charge densities have a negative diffusion constant once the chemical potential exceeds $2\sqrt{2}\pi T$ at temperature $T$ [gladden2025]. The unstable modes are differences between the three gauge fields coupled to the scalars, absent from a theory with the metric and one gauge field, so at low temperature the gauge theory with equal chemical potentials is not described by the brane with equal charges [gladden2025].

related.text: The hole of five dimensions with no cosmological constant, $L \to \infty$, and a horizon that is a 3-sphere. With the gauging only its metric function changes, by the term in $L$ [behrndt1999].
This black hole with no charge and no cosmological constant, $q_1 = q_2 = q_3 = 0$ and $L \to \infty$.
The charged black hole of anti-de Sitter space in four dimensions. With its three charges equal this hole is the same kind of hole in five dimensions, with constant scalars [myers2001].
The black hole of anti-de Sitter space with no charge, in four dimensions. With no charge this hole is its counterpart in five dimensions [behrndt1999].
Black holes of anti-de Sitter space in four dimensions with flat and hyperbolic horizons. These holes have the same three kinds of horizon in five dimensions, $k = 1$, $0$, and $-1$ [behrndt1999].

The throat of a stack of three-branes, anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times a 5-sphere. With the branes spinning in three planes, away from extremality, the region near them is this hole with a flat horizon [cvetic1999embed].

Smooth geometries of ten dimensions drawn as droplets on a plane. Lifted to ten dimensions, the solutions here with $\mu = 0$ are superstars, whose naked singularities Robert C. Myers and Øyvind Tafjord traced to giant gravitons [myers2001].

The supersymmetric hole of five dimensions in flat space with its charges equal, set spinning. In anti-de Sitter space no static supersymmetric hole of this kind has a regular horizon [behrndt1998bps].
The vacuum of these holes, in four dimensions. With $\mu = q_1 = q_2 = q_3 = 0$ and $k = 1$ the metric here is anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions.

coordinates.convention: We use the radius $r$ of Behrndt, Cvetič, and Sabra [behrndt1999] and the angles $(\chi, \theta, \phi)$ of the 3-sphere, with $t$ having dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, so $\dot{t}$ in the geodesic equations means $d(ct)/d\lambda$. The mass is $M = \pi c^2\left(3\mu + 2q_1 + 2q_2 + 2q_3\right)/(8G)$, with $G$ Newton's constant in five dimensions [behrndt1999].
